newsitem.title: INDIA: New Bombay stocks index seen helping funds flow.
newsitem.headline: New Bombay stocks index seen helping funds flow.

text.p: The revamped 30-share benchmark sensitive index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) could help attract more funds to India from global fund managers, investment firm Birla Marlin Securities said on the weekend.
"It could encourage allocation of more funds to India," Mukarram Bhagat, the firm's head of research.
A study on the revised index by Birla Marlin analyst K.R. Sudhakar said volatility in the new index would be much lower compared to the earlier index.
"Given the low volatility, the risk perceptions of the investors would be lower than before," Sudhakar said.
The required rate of return on equity investments in India would also fall as the risk perception comes down, he said.
"Fund managers allocating country exposure levels may rework allocation, taking into account the lower volatility and hence, reduced risk levels," the study said.
The study was based on statistics for the old and the revised sensex for the period May 1994 to May 1996 on the basis of returns obtained from the BSE, it said.
"As on 16 August 1996, the market was trading at 11.2 percent 1996/97 (April-March) earnings (Marlin estimates) of the new index," the study said.
"This means that the market benchmark has become cheaper with a lower risk portfolio."
The BSE revamped the 30-share index last month to make it more representative of changes in market capitalisation in recent years.
The new index has several large state-run firms which were listed on the exchange after the government divested some of its holdings as part of the economic reforms launched in 1991.
